Thanks for the reply, indeed your approach works exactly as I want.

is there a way to have the lines colored?

Ale


On Oct 28, 2014, at 17:49, Dennis Murphy <djm...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi:
>
> (1) I would have gone about the color issue differently. I would have
> plotted all the points, but increased the size and changed the color
> of the significant ones. To that end, you would need an indicator to
> distinguish the significant from non-significant points. In that case,
> you would have two legends: one for year and one for significance.
> (2) To answer your question directly, put color = "red" inside of
> aes(); that will produce a one-element legend with label "red". The
> problem is that you'll likely get an error message since you'd then be
> trying to map the same aesthetic (color) to two different variables,
> and ggplot2 does not allow that.
> (3) I don't see why you're creating legends for size and shape since
> you never mapped a variable to either aesthetic. I do, however, see
> size set to 1 in geom_line().
> (4) The group aesthetic plays no role so you can just eliminate it.
>
> It appears that you were trying to combine the years as lines and the
> red dot together in one legend. You can do this with a bit of effort
> in base graphics with the legend() function, but that won't work in
> ggplot2 by design. I would suggest that you apply my suggestion in (1)
> for the points and map year to linetype, ending up with two legends,
> something like
>
>
> # significance indicator
> DF$sig <- as.factor(!is.na(DF$V4))
>
> ggplot(DF, aes(x=dist.class.1/1000, y=Moran.correlog)) +
> geom_line(aes(linetype = factor(year)), size = 1, color = "blue") +
> geom_point(aes(color = sig, size = sig)) +
> labs(linetype = "Year", color = "p < 0.05", size = "p < 0.05") +
> scale_color_manual(values = c("black", "red")) +
> scale_size_manual(values = c(2, 5))
>
> Dennis

>

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: correlogram plot with ggplot
parts:
The only way I can think of is to use point shape 21 and then map fill
to the points, which then frees you to map color to the lines,
something like (untested)

... +
geom_line(aes(linetype = factor(year), color = factor(year)), size = 1) +
geom_point(aes(size = sig, fill = sig), shape = 21) +
... +
scale_fill_manual(values = c("black", "red")) + # note change to fill
scale_size_manual(values = c(2, 5))

The reason for using shape 21 (circle) is that shapes 21-25 allow you
to map fill color to points. You probably need to add color = "year"
and fill = "p < 0.05" to labs() as well.

Dennis
